hints: Let $t=\tan x$, use $\tan(x-60^\circ)=\frac{t-\sqrt3}{1+\sqrt3t}$, and write $2\cot x$ as $2/t$.
Cross-multiply and collect terms to form the required quadratic in $t$.
Solve the quadratic for both values of $\tan x$.
For each tangent value, find every angle in $0^\circ\le x\le180^\circ$ and reject any value at which the original expression is undefined.
walkthrough:
Apply the compound angle subtraction identity $\tan(A - B) = \dfrac{\tan A - \tan B}{1 + \tan A\tan B}$ with $A = x$ and $B = 60^{\circ}$:
$$\tan 60^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}$$
$$\tan(x - 60^{\circ}) = \dfrac{\tan x - \tan 60^{\circ}}{1 + \tan x\tan 60^{\circ}} = \dfrac{\tan x - \sqrt{3}}{1 + \sqrt{3}\tan x}$$

Express $2\cot x$ in terms of $\tan x$:
$$\cot x = \dfrac{1}{\tan x} \implies 2\cot x = \dfrac{2}{\tan x}$$

Equate the two expressions:
$$\dfrac{\tan x - \sqrt{3}}{1 + \sqrt{3}\tan x} = \dfrac{2}{\tan x}$$

Multiply both sides by $\tan x(1 + \sqrt{3}\tan x)$ to clear fractions:
$$\tan x(\tan x - \sqrt{3}) = 2(1 + \sqrt{3}\tan x)$$
$$\tan^2 x - \sqrt{3}\tan x = 2 + 2\sqrt{3}\tan x$$

Collect all terms onto the left-hand side to form a three-term quadratic equation in $\tan x$:
$$\tan^2 x - \sqrt{3}\tan x - 2\sqrt{3}\tan x - 2 = 0$$
$$\tan^2 x - 3\sqrt{3}\tan x - 2 = 0$$

Solve the quadratic equation using the quadratic formula with $a = 1, b = -3\sqrt{3}, c = -2$:
$$b^2 - 4ac = (-3\sqrt{3})^2 - 4(1)(-2) = (9 \times 3) - (-8) = 27 + 8 = 35$$
$$\tan x = \dfrac{-(-3\sqrt{3}) \pm \sqrt{35}}{2(1)} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3} \pm \sqrt{35}}{2}$$

Compute the arithmetic values of the two roots:
$$3\sqrt{3} \approx 3 \times 1.7320508 = 5.1961524$$
$$\sqrt{35} \approx 5.9160798$$
$$\text{Root 1: } \tan x = \dfrac{5.1961524 + 5.9160798}{2} = \dfrac{11.1122322}{2} \approx 5.556116$$
$$\text{Root 2: } \tan x = \dfrac{5.1961524 - 5.9160798}{2} = \dfrac{-0.7199274}{2} \approx -0.359964$$

Calculate the angles in the given range $0^{\circ} \leqslant x \leqslant 180^{\circ}$:
$$\text{For } \tan x \approx 5.556116: \quad x = \tan^{-1}(5.556116) \approx 79.799^{\circ} \approx 79.8^{\circ}$$
$$\text{For } \tan x \approx -0.359964: \quad \text{basic acute angle } \alpha = \tan^{-1}(0.359964) \approx 19.799^{\circ}$$
$$x = 180^{\circ} - 19.799^{\circ} = 160.201^{\circ} \approx 160.2^{\circ}$$
$$x = 79.8^{\circ}, \quad 160.2^{\circ}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Replace $2cot x$ by $2/\tan x$. Reduces to $\tan^2x-3\sqrt{3} \tan x-2=0$, or equivalent three-term equation. The solved value is x=79.8°, 160.2°.
